n1: The binding is incomplete (`(...)`) and the node’s criterion only checks the mug’s final position. In the edited image, the mug on the right is to the right of the headphones, but the original blue mug remains as a blurred/ghosted object on the left and another mug appears near the headphones. Thus the traces’ confident “complete” judgment may be overlooking whether the requested mug was actually moved, rather than duplicated or left behind; the reference `partial` is an aggregate constraint, not proof of a specific atomic interpretation. Repair the binding to identify the mug from the source (the blue mug left of the headphones), and make the decision criterion compare source and edited images for that same object, distinguishing genuine movement toward/right of the headphones from persistence, duplication, or an ambiguous identity. Preserve an unknown/unresolved outcome when identity or movement cannot be established; do not infer partial progress merely from low confidence or variation. The five identical, high-confidence traces indicate a systematic criterion/evidence blind spot, not a transport or dependency failure.

The node’s criterion only checks whether the mug ends up right of the headphones, so it treats a completed relocation as complete even when the edited image also retains an extra mug at the original location. The source has one mug left of the headphones; the edit appears to leave a blurred mug-shaped remnant there while adding a mug on the right. Make the decision explicitly compare source and edited images and assess both requested progress and whether the original mug was actually moved rather than duplicated/left behind; distinguish that case from a clean relocation. Preserve an unknown outcome if the remnant or object identity cannot be judged reliably. The five high-confidence, identical traces show a systematic criterion/binding gap, not transport or dependency failure; the reference ‘partial’ constrains the aggregate but does not by itself establish the remnant as ground truth.
